title: Bounded-below pseudo-coherent complexes are perfect if all prime localizations are perfect
statement: Let $B$ be any commutative ring and let $K\in D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Suppose there is an integer $c$ such that $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i<c$. For each prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$, let $B_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization of $B$ at $B\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and form $K_{\mathfrak q}=K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B_{\mathfrak q}$ by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. If $K_{\mathfrak q}$ is perfect over $B_{\mathfrak q}$ for every $\mathfrak q$, then $K$ is perfect over $B$, that is, isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $B$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. The bounds of the perfect complexes at different primes need not be uniform. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 068W, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, implication (2) to (1) under the bounded-below hypothesis in its final sentence.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $F^\bullet$ of $K$ by pseudo-coherence. A finite free module is flat: tensoring a module injection with $B^n$ gives the same injection in each of its $n$ coordinates. The bounded-flat K-flat lemma therefore applies to $F^\bullet$, and also to the bounded-above finite-free complex $F^\bullet\otimes_BB_{\mathfrak q}$ over $B_{\mathfrak q}$. The fixed-second-factor derived-tensor functor thus computes $K_{\mathfrak q}$ by $F^\bullet\otimes_BB_{\mathfrak q}$ and computes the two residue extensions by their ordinary tensor complexes. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$; the map $B\to k$ factors through $B_{\mathfrak q}$ because every element outside $\mathfrak q$ maps to a nonzero element of $k$. Degreewise the maps $(x\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes uv$ and $x\otimes v\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes v$ are inverse balanced linear maps and commute with the differentials. Consequently they give an isomorphism $K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}k\simeq K_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{B_{\mathfrak q}}^{\mathbf L}k$ in $D(k)$.

source.place: Tag 068W, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, final proof paragraph; Tags 064K, 066W and 0BYP for its inputs.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$. By hypothesis $K_{\mathfrak q}$ is perfect. Apply preservation of perfect complexes under derived scalar extension to $B_{\mathfrak q}\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Together with step 1 this makes $K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ perfect. By the definition of perfect, choose a bounded finite-projective representative of this fibre and a lower bound $a_{\mathfrak q}$ for its terms. Its cohomology is zero in degrees $i<a_{\mathfrak q}$, since the representing term in degree $i$ is zero. In particular $d_i=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}H^i(K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak q))=0$ for $i<a_{\mathfrak q}$. The chosen integer can depend on $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 068W, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, final proof paragraph; Tags 064K, 066W and 0BYP for its inputs.

proof.text: Apply the bounded-below residue-model lemma to $R=B$, the prime $\mathfrak q$, and $a=a_{\mathfrak q}$. Its pseudo-coherence and bounded-below hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses on $K$; step 2 supplies its residue-dimension vanishing. It yields $f_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$ and a bounded finite-free representative of $K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B_{f_{\mathfrak q}}$. Finite free modules are finitely generated projective, so this localized object is perfect. Thus every prime lies in a principal open $D(f_{\mathfrak q})$ on which $K$ has a perfect scalar extension.

source.place: Tag 068W, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, final proof paragraph; Tags 064K, 066W and 0BYP for its inputs.

proof.text: The principal opens $D(f_{\mathfrak q})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Quasi-compactness of the spectrum gives a finite subcover $D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_r)$, and the principal-cover criterion says these $f_j$ generate the unit ideal. Each $K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B_{f_j}$ is perfect by step 3. The principal-cover gluing lemma therefore gives that $K$ is perfect over $B$, with the bounded finite-projective meaning in the statement. The gluing lemma allows $r=0$, so the empty spectrum (the zero ring) is included. Only the finite cover, not any prescribed uniform bound on the primewise representatives, is used.
